// diagnostic

E0406

Old `Result<T, E>` is a retired fallible type spelling

What

Old `Result<T, E>` is a retired fallible type spelling

Why

The result surface now puts `?` before an optional success type and `!` before its error domain

Fix

Write `?T !E`, `T !(E1 | E2)`, or omit the contract for implicit `Err`

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0406: tests/ui/result_old_syntax.stderr.

Error [E0406]: `Result<T, E>` is old Jet error syntax
  --> tests/ui/result_old_syntax.jet:5:11
    |
  5 | fn f() => Result<Int, E> {
    |           ^^^^^^
 Why: fallible Jet types use a success type and a prefixed error contract
 Fix: write `?T !E`, `T !(E1 | E2)`, or omit the contract for implicit `Err`
